id: GB-05 GSD work through Edit and Write, and the transcript folder, as Claude Code on Windows records them
note: Sitting 6, log 21. Claude Code on Windows records an Edit or Write file_path in drive form with backslashes (C:\x\.planning\STATE.md); the GSD walk matched only '.planning/' after a leading '/', so GSD work done through Edit and Write was never seen there. Such a path, in drive form with backslashes or slashes, is now read in its /c/ form (util::posix_form) before the match. Claude Code names a session's project folder from the cwd it sees, every character outside [A-Za-z0-9] made '-' (C:\winkit-x6 is C--winkit-x6); the folder was looked up from the /c/ form only (-c-winkit-x6). Under MSYS or Cygwin perl the Windows form of each folder (util::win_form) is tried first, then the old slug and the one-folder fallback. Seams: STORE_TEST_OS=msys, STORE_TEST_CYGDRIVE (C: reads as $TMP/cyg/c, and $TMP/cyg/c back as C:). Two project folders hold the session's transcript in the folder steps, so the one-folder fallback cannot pick one. The last steps drop STORE_TEST_CYGDRIVE and run under a perl first on PATH that defines Cygwin::win_to_posix_path and Cygwin::posix_to_win_path as Git Bash's perl has them (as RF-9 does), so the sub production calls is the one read. On macOS and Linux (STORE_TEST_OS=linux) a drive path is still no GSD path and the folder is looked up as before. Sitting 8: the checkout's toplevel came from the real git, and Git for Windows prints the real temp folder in drive form (C:/<tmp>/cyg/c/w/repo), which the stand-in read as a folder that does not exist, so the checkout had no GSD root and the re-entry got a stray --cwd. The step that checks the re-entry without --cwd now runs under GB-03's git stand-in (drive-git, which prints that path as C:/w/repo), in front of a second stub (win-git) that prints git's POSIX paths in drive form as Git for Windows does, so macOS and Linux run that step as the PC does. The other steps keep the real git: under STORE_TEST_OS=linux and STORE_TEST_NO_CYGWIN the not-found steps need its POSIX toplevel.

setup.script:
out=$(PATH=${PATH#*:} git "$@"); rc=$?
[ -n "$out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's#\([A-Za-z]:\)\{0,1\}/[^ ]*/cyg/c/#C:/#g'
exit $rc

out=$(PATH=${PATH#*:} git "$@"); rc=$?
[ -n "$out" ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed 's#^/#C:/#'
exit $rc
